description: Simulates the Slack Web API including chat, conversations, users, reactions, pins, files, and more. Every method answers GET and POST, and arguments are accepted as a query string, a form body, multipart, text/plain or JSON, as Slack accepts them. A name that is not a method answers unknown_method before authentication, and every error repeats its code in the x-slack-failure header. The caller is identified from the token, which may be sent in the Authorization header or a form body field: any well-formed xoxb-, xoxp- or xapp- token is accepted, seeded tokens speak for their own user, and auth.revoke revokes. api.test answers without a token. conversations.list, conversations.history, conversations.replies, conversations.members, users.list, users.conversations, reactions.list and chat.scheduledMessages.list page with a cursor and a limit, with next_cursor empty on the last page, invalid_cursor for a cursor that does not compute, and an unusable limit adjusted. Empty lists are answered as [], never null. A state snapshot keeps every store, including pins, bookmarks, usergroups, presence, bots, custom emoji, deleted messages, the ts counter and the simulated clock, and loading it restores the state exactly, empty stores included; a seed file replaces only the stores it names. The bot user and the default user that unseeded tokens speak for are workspace users, with the bot B_BOT of app A_SIM. The external file upload runs end to end on the emulator: files.getUploadURLExternal requires filename and length and returns an upload URL on the host the client called, the bytes are posted there, files carry a mimetype and filetype taken from the extension, and files.completeUploadExternal gives each file a url_private and url_private_download on the same host that serve its bytes to a caller with a token, and posts a file_share message, with initial_comment as its text and thread_ts honoured, to each channel in channel_id or channels and emits it as a message event. files.completeUploadExternal answers file_not_found for a file whose bytes never reached the upload URL. files.list lists completed uploads, filters by channel, user, types, ts_from and ts_to, and pages with count and page. views.publish keeps one Home tab view per user, replaced on each publish and guarded by its hash, and views.update finds a view by view_id or external_id; views.open and views.push keep the modal they open, without checking trigger_id. oauth.v2.access is called without a token, takes the client credentials by HTTP Basic or as arguments, and exchanges any authorization code once for a new bot token that the rest of the API accepts. conversations.open resumes the existing direct or multi-person message for the same users, answers a direct message with a D id that names the other user, and returns only the channel id unless return_im is set. Reactions and pins belong to the caller, a message is pinned once, and reactions, pins and bookmarks answer channel_not_found for a channel that does not exist; bookmarks.add takes a link bookmark with a title and an http or https URL, bookmarks.edit refuses a link that is not a URL with invalid_link, and bookmarks.edit and bookmarks.remove answer not_found for a bookmark that is unknown or in another channel. conversations.join on a channel the caller is already in answers ok with the warning already_in_channel and response_metadata.warnings. chat.postMessage reflects username, icon_emoji as icons.emoji, attachments, metadata and reply_broadcast, refuses an archived channel with is_archived, and a bot's post carries bot_id, app_id and bot_profile, in the message and its event; and chat.getPermalink answers message_not_found for an unknown ts. users.setPresence answers invalid_presence for anything but auto or away. Every method answers invalid_arguments for an argument of the wrong type (users.profile.set profile fields excepted), and a number or boolean sent as a string in a JSON body is taken as its value. conversations.list and users.conversations list public channels by default and filter by types, and list a private channel, direct message or multi-person message only to its members. conversations.history and conversations.replies answer channel_not_found for a channel that does not exist, and replies answers thread_not_found for a ts that is not a message in the channel. A user group always carries is_usergroup: true, a disabled group carries its date_delete, and usergroups.list leaves disabled groups out unless include_disabled is set. With a Request URL set through --webhook-url or POST /admin/events/config, chat.postMessage, chat.meMessage, chat.delete, reactions.add, files.completeUploadExternal and scheduled-message delivery are delivered as Events API event_callbacks, a message event carrying the message's subtype, files and attachments, and conversations.join, invite, leave and kick as member_joined_channel and member_left_channel, signed with X-Slack-Signature over v0:{timestamp}:{body}; a delivery that fails is retried up to three times with x-slack-retry-num and x-slack-retry-reason unless the receiver answers x-slack-no-retry: 1. Setting the Request URL through POST /admin/events/config makes Slack's url_verification handshake, and POST /admin/reset clears the delivery log and queued events. Messages, edits, channels, topics, purposes, files, memberships, profiles and presence belong to the user the token speaks for, and a channel's is_member says whether that user is in it. chat.postMessage, chat.postEphemeral, chat.update and chat.scheduleMessage take markdown_text alone, answering markdown_text_conflict with text or blocks and no_text with no content. Only a message's author updates it (cant_update_message); a bot deletes only its own messages and a user their own, an admin or owner anyone's (cant_delete_message); an update with text and no blocks drops the blocks. chat.scheduleMessage refuses a post_at in the past (time_in_past) or more than 120 days ahead (time_too_far), answers the message as a delayed_message, and posts it in its channel or thread once post_at passes on the simulated clock, except a message with metadata, which never posts; chat.scheduledMessages.list shows a caller the messages its principal scheduled, by channel, oldest and latest. conversations.history and conversations.replies honour oldest, latest and inclusive. conversations.setTopic answers the conversation, and setPurpose the conversation and the purpose; both refuse an archived conversation. reactions.list lists a message once per reaction of the user, with its channel, and leaves out deleted messages. users.profile.set takes a user token and sets the documented profile fields and custom fields, by profile or by name and value; another user's profile only by an admin or owner. usergroups.create requires a name and refuses a name or handle already in use. chat.unfurl checks the message, its links and the unfurls; bots.info answers a bot by ID; users.identity answers a user token's identity; emoji.list lists seeded custom emoji; team.info answers the workspace object. conversations.invite answers user_not_found or cant_invite_self, with each failure in errors, and invites nobody unless force is set, and no_user with no users; invite, join, leave, chat.postEphemeral and chat.meMessage refuse an archived conversation with is_archived, and chat.postEphemeral answers user_not_in_channel for a user outside the channel. conversations.kick refuses the caller with cant_kick_self. conversations.mark checks ts and membership and moves the caller's read cursor, shown as last_read by conversations.info; conversations.close closes a direct or multi-person message for the caller, answering no_op and already_closed when it is closed already, and conversations.open reopens it. pins.list requires its channel and shows each pinned message as it is now, leaving out deleted ones. usergroups.users.update answers no_users_provided for an empty list and failed_for_some_users for a user outside the workspace. A file's timestamp is its creation time.

lifecycle.changelog:
First release of the Slack app emulator. It targets the Slack Web API as documented on 2026-09-26, as a newly created granular Slack app sees it. Slack does not version its API.

### Supported
- 73 Web API methods across auth, chat, conversations, users, reactions, pins, files (external upload), bookmarks, views, emoji, team, bots, usergroups and oauth.v2.access, with Slack's documented errors
- Events API HTTP delivery for message, message_deleted, reaction_added, member_joined_channel and member_left_channel, signed, retried, with the url_verification handshake
- Cursor pagination, scheduled messages on a simulated clock, and state snapshots, reset and seeding through /admin

### Verified
- Official SDKs @slack/web-api 8.1.1 and slack_sdk 3.44.1: 32 of 32 scenario cases against the app emulator
- Through LocalStack: 28 of 32. The two file upload cases fail (known issues below); the two event cases were not run, because the check's receiver was not reachable from the LocalStack container
- Live comparison with Slack: not run

### Not modelled
- Methods outside the supported use cases, and methods Slack retired, answer unknown_method. Every deliberate difference from Slack is listed in twin-slack/divergences.json

### Known issues
- Through LocalStack, file upload and download links point at an address the client cannot reach, so external file uploads fail with both SDKs, pending a LocalStack fix
- Once that is fixed, file uploads from the Python slack_sdk (files_upload_v2) still arrive corrupted through LocalStack, pending a second LocalStack fix
- Run directly, without LocalStack, file uploads work with both SDKs
